### Example 1 · Page 4

Write $\sinh 2$ in terms of the exponential function.

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show solution</summary>

Since

$$
\sinh x=\frac{e^x-e^{-x}}2,
$$

putting $x=2$ gives

$$
\boxed{\sinh 2=\frac{e^2-e^{-2}}2}.
$$

</details>
<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="hyp-example-1"> Completed</label>
:::

::: {.study-card}
### Example 2 · Page 4

Find the value of $\sinh 2$ to 3 decimal places.

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show solution</summary>

Using the hyperbolic function on a calculator, or substituting into the exponential form,

$$
\boxed{\sinh 2=3.627}\ \text{to 3 d.p.}
$$

</details>
<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="hyp-example-2"> Completed</label>
:::

::: {.study-card}
### Example 3 · Page 5

Find the exact value of $\operatorname{sech}(\ln 2)$.

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show solution</summary>

Using $\operatorname{sech}x=\dfrac2{e^x+e^{-x}}$ with $x=\ln2$,

$$
\operatorname{sech}(\ln2)=\frac2{2+\frac12}
=\frac2{\frac52}
=\boxed{\frac45}.
$$

</details>
<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="hyp-example-3"> Completed</label>
:::

::: {.study-card}
### Example 4 · Page 5

Find the value(s) of $x$, to 3 decimal places, for which $\cosh x=2$.

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show solution</summary>

Using $\cosh x=\dfrac{e^x+e^{-x}}2$,

$$
\frac{e^x+e^{-x}}2=2
\;\Longrightarrow\;
e^{2x}-4e^x+1=0.
$$

The quadratic formula gives

$$
e^x=2\pm\sqrt3=3.732\ldots\ \text{or}\ 0.267\ldots,
$$

so

$$
\boxed{x=\ln(3.732\ldots)=1.317\ \text{or}\ x=\ln(0.267\ldots)=-1.317}
$$

to 3 decimal places.

</details>
<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="hyp-example-4"> Completed</label>
:::

::: {.study-card}

### Example 11 · Page 9

Determine whether the trigonometric identity $\cos^2x+\sin^2x=1$ can be converted to $\cosh^2x+\sinh^2x=1$ for hyperbolic functions.

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show solution</summary>

Substitute the exponential forms:

$$
\cosh^2x+\sinh^2x
=\left(\frac{e^x+e^{-x}}2\right)^2+\left(\frac{e^x-e^{-x}}2\right)^2.
$$

Expanding,

$$
\frac{e^{2x}+2+e^{-2x}}4+\frac{e^{2x}-2+e^{-2x}}4
=\frac{e^{2x}+e^{-2x}}2.
$$

This is not equal to $1$, so

$$
\boxed{\cosh^2x+\sinh^2x\neq1}.
$$

The correct identity is $\cosh^2x-\sinh^2x=1$.

</details>
<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="hyp-example-11"> Completed</label>
:::

::: {.study-card}
### Example 12 · Page 10

Show that $\cosh(A+B)=\cosh A\cosh B+\sinh A\sinh B$.

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show solution</summary>

Substitute the exponential forms:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\cosh A\cosh B+\sinh A\sinh B
&=\left(\frac{e^A+e^{-A}}2\right)\left(\frac{e^B+e^{-B}}2\right)
+\left(\frac{e^A-e^{-A}}2\right)\left(\frac{e^B-e^{-B}}2\right)\\
&=\frac{e^{A+B}+e^{A-B}+e^{-A+B}+e^{-A-B}}4\\
&\quad+\frac{e^{A+B}-e^{A-B}-e^{-A+B}+e^{-A-B}}4\\
&=\frac{2e^{A+B}+2e^{-(A+B)}}4\\
&=\frac{e^{A+B}+e^{-(A+B)}}2\\
&=\cosh(A+B).
\end{aligned}
$$

The related results

$$
\cosh(A-B)=\cosh A\cosh B-\sinh A\sinh B,
$$

$$
\sinh(A\pm B)=\sinh A\cosh B\pm\cosh A\sinh B
$$

follow in the same way.

</details>
<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="hyp-example-12"> Completed</label>
:::

::: {.study-card}
### Example 13 · Page 11

Given that $\cosh x=3$, find the value of:

**(a)** $\sinh x$;

**(b)** $\tanh x$.

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show solution</summary>

**(a)** Using $\cosh^2x-\sinh^2x=1$,

$$
9-\sinh^2x=1
\;\Longrightarrow\;
\sinh^2x=8,
$$

so

$$
\boxed{\sinh x=\pm2\sqrt2}.
$$

**(b)** Using $\tanh x=\dfrac{\sinh x}{\cosh x}$,

$$
\boxed{\tanh x=\pm\frac{2\sqrt2}3}.
$$

</details>
<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="hyp-example-13"> Completed</label>
:::

::: {.study-card}
### Example 14 · Page 13

Sketch the graph and state the domain of $y=\sinh^{-1}x$.

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show solution</summary>

The graph of $y=\sinh^{-1}x$ is the reflection of $y=\sinh x$ in the line $y=x$. Since $\sinh x$ is one-to-one on $\mathbb R$,

$$
\boxed{\text{domain: }x\in\mathbb R}.
$$

{{< include figures/hyperbolic/graph-arsinh.svg >}}

</details>
<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="hyp-example-14"> Completed</label>
:::

### Example 15 · Page 14

State a possible domain of $\cosh^{-1}x$ and sketch the graph for your chosen domain. What are the implications for the domain of $y=\cosh x$ for $y=\cosh^{-1}x$ to be a function?

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show solution</summary>

$\cosh x$ is many-to-one, so its domain is restricted to $x\geqslant0$. The inverse function then has

$$
\boxed{\text{domain: }x\geqslant1}.
$$

{{< include figures/hyperbolic/graph-arcosh.svg >}}

</details>
<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="hyp-example-15"> Completed</label>
:::

### Example 16 · Page 14

Write $\sinh^{-1}x$ in logarithmic form.

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show solution</summary>

Let $y=\sinh^{-1}x$, so $x=\sinh y$. Then

$$
x=\frac{e^y-e^{-y}}2
\;\Longrightarrow\;
e^{2y}-2xe^y-1=0.
$$

The quadratic formula gives

$$
e^y=x\pm\sqrt{x^2+1}.
$$

The negative sign gives a negative value of $e^y$, which is impossible, so

$$
\boxed{\sinh^{-1}x=\ln\left(x+\sqrt{x^2+1}\right)}.
$$

</details>
<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="hyp-example-16"> Completed</label>
:::

::: {.study-card}
### Example 17 · Page 15

Write $\sinh^{-1}2$ in logarithmic form.

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show solution</summary>

Substitute $x=2$ into $\sinh^{-1}x=\ln\left(x+\sqrt{x^2+1}\right)$:

$$
\boxed{\sinh^{-1}2=\ln\left(2+\sqrt5\right)}.
$$

</details>
<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="hyp-example-17"> Completed</label>
:::
